question: Are the model's SAMPLED COORDINATES chemically sane, measured directly against real tmQM geometry without RDKit?
why_this_was_measured: Every quality number on disk for free generation is computed by RDKit FROM the decoded molecular graph -- QED, SA, single_fragment_ratio, and the 3D-embeddability rate. None of them reads the model's coordinates. So the geometry the velocity field actually produces has never been measured on its own terms.

cohort.templates: 24 tmQM val clouds, composition only (coordinates discarded, re-drawn from noise)
cohort.mode: eval() + torch.no_grad(), forward ODE integration only -- NO TRAINING
cohort.caveat: SMOKE SCALE. 24 clouds, 20 steps, one checkpoint, one seed. Directionally unambiguous, not a settled number.

headline: THE SAMPLED GEOMETRY IS BADLY DEFECTIVE, AND NO EXISTING METRIC SEES IT. All 24 generated clouds contain at least one hard steric clash; zero of 24 real tmQM clouds do. The mean closest interatomic contact is 0.570 A in generated geometry against 1.172 A in real tmQM -- a bond-length-scale contact, not a non-bonded one.

definitions.hard_clash_pair: an atom pair closer than 0.7 * (rcov_i + rcov_j). Covalent radii from Cordero et al. 2008. Such a pair cannot be a bond and is not a plausible non-bonded contact in tmQM.
definitions.metal_ligand: distance from each metal to its 4 nearest atoms.
definitions.note: These are GEOMETRY metrics computed with plain torch -- no RDKit, no bond head, no graph. That is the point: they are independent of every metric the project already reports.

reading: Generated clouds are globally the right SIZE (radius of gyration 3.57 vs 3.81 A, median pair distance 4.71 vs 5.00 A) but locally collapsed: atoms sit almost on top of each other while the overall extent is about right.

The metal-ligand contacts are the worst: mean closest contact 1.234 A against 1.953 A in real tmQM. A real metal-ligand bond is 2.0-2.4 A. The generated geometry places first-shell ligands INSIDE the metal's own covalent radius.
Real tmQM scores exactly 0 hard clashes across all 24 clouds, so the clash measure is not an artifact of the threshold.
why_L1_did_not_see_this: BLK-C-L1 measured the REGRESSION RESIDUAL on real tmQM geometries (does the velocity field predict the right velocity on well-formed input?). It never looked at what the sampler produces from NOISE. Those are different questions, and the first one came back healthy.
consequence_for_the_diagnosis: The velocity field fits real geometry reasonably well (L1: loss tracks the target's own scale, no subset starved) AND still emits collapsed geometry from noise. Both are true. A model can score well on its training distribution and still be wrong at generation time -- which is precisely the well-known train/test mismatch of conditional generative models, and it is invisible to every metric currently on disk.
consequence_for_L5: NONE for the embeddability number. RDKit's EmbedMolecule discards these coordinates entirely (see cfm_embed_failure_localisation.json), so improving them cannot move the 18.8% figure. The two findings are about different objects and do not compete.
consequence_for_L3_guidance: This is the ONE finding that gives the sampling-time guidance family a real target. The repulsion core is the single force component every cited method shares, and there is now a measured, large, unambiguous coordinate-level defect for it to act on. See the guided arm in cfm_l3_guidance_ab.json.
